bug_semantics: An authenticated non-site-admin with the perm_template permission can GET the event-template add page (or edit a template writable by that user's organisation). EventTemplatesController::__setBuilderConfig() queried every enabled Galaxy row without Galaxy visibility conditions, grouped the results by type, retained each type and description, and embedded that data in window.ET_BUILDER_CONFIG.multipickerSources. Consequently, the builder response disclosed metadata for enabled private distribution-0 galaxies owned by other organisations.
flaw_origin: Commit 47bf71cc78d13c06e1eaa4d9842e6f94ddce4bea introduced the galaxy-type picker and, in the same atomic feature commit, first added the server-side Galaxy->find('all') with only 'Galaxy.enabled' => true. It did not call Galaxy::buildConditions() or otherwise restrict by the requesting user's organisation/distribution before exposing Galaxy.type and Galaxy.description to the browser.
ai_marker: BIC commit object contains the exact trailer 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>'. git cat-file -p also shows human author and committer iglocska <andras.iklody@gmail.com>; the Claude Co-Authored-By trailer is nevertheless explicit commit-object AI co-authorship.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3636-3mqq-q7x9 describes non-site-admin access to private galaxies from other organisations through event-template creation, names leaked galaxy type/description metadata, and references d3adfe1a097dd4b403364e9af34e208660eeec1a; its affected/patched version fields are Unknown.

git show 47bf71cc78d13c06e1eaa4d9842e6f94ddce4bea -- app/Controller/EventTemplatesController.php shows the BIC adding __setBuilderConfig()'s Galaxy->find('all') with conditions array('Galaxy.enabled' => true), fields Galaxy.type and Galaxy.description, grouping by Galaxy.type, and set('galaxyTypesAvailable', ...). The same commit wires those values into the event-template builder's browser configuration.

git log -S"'Galaxy.enabled' => true" -- app/Controller/EventTemplatesController.php resolves the first addition to 47bf71cc78d13c06e1eaa4d9842e6f94ddce4bea. git log -L over the added galaxy-result processing also traces those lines to that commit. git cat-file -p shows it is a normal one-parent commit, parent 66f278bb2be0e8183d56eede615d7cc370f38303, so no squash/member decomposition is needed.

Immediate-parent tree verification: git grep -n -E 'galaxyTypesAvailable|Galaxy\.enabled|loadModel\(.Galaxy.' 66f278bb2be0e8183d56eede615d7cc370f38303 -- app/Controller/EventTemplatesController.php returned no matches (exit 1), while the parent-to-BIC diff adds the entire unrestricted Galaxy query and result exposure. The vulnerable mechanism is therefore absent from the direct parent.

Authorization/reachability: app/Controller/Component/ACLComponent.php grants eventTemplates/add and eventTemplates/edit to perm_template users; EventTemplatesController.php calls __setBuilderConfig() on GET add and GET edit. Thus a low-privileged authenticated template author can receive the leaked picker configuration; edit additionally enforces own-organisation ownership of the template, which does not constrain the separate Galaxy query.

The advisory-referenced d3adfe1a097dd4b403364e9af34e208660eeec1a is an incomplete attempted repair: it adds an OR condition containing 'Galaxy.distribution' > 0, which PHP evaluates before building the query rather than expressing a CakePHP field comparison. The later effective fix 8aa2bb6d1af6e8c57c8d8437cf203acb8bce7a53 explicitly identifies that expression as an always-true PHP comparison and replaces the hand-written condition with $this->Galaxy->buildConditions($this->Auth->user()). Galaxy.php's buildConditions() permits site admins globally and otherwise limits results to default galaxies, the user's org, or non-private distributions 1-3.

Version boundary from repository tags: git tag --contains 47bf71cc78d13c06e1eaa4d9842e6f94ddce4bea starts at v2.5.37, and git grep finds no Galaxy.enabled query in v2.5.36 but finds it in v2.5.37/v2.5.38. d3adfe1a097dd4b403364e9af34e208660eeec1a first appears in v2.5.39, which still contains the malformed comparison. 8aa2bb6d1af6e8c57c8d8437cf203acb8bce7a53 first appears in v2.5.40; git grep finds the canonical buildConditions call in v2.5.40 and not v2.5.39. Therefore the shipped vulnerable boundary is v2.5.37 through v2.5.39, with the effective patched boundary at v2.5.40.

git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms both the BIC and the advisory-referenced attempted fix are ancestors of 8aa2bb6d1af6e8c57c8d8437cf203acb8bce7a53. git show/cat-file of the BIC itself provides the only AI attribution used here: the exact Claude Opus Co-Authored-By trailer on the commit that first wrote the flawed query.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when 47bf71cc78d13c06e1eaa4d9842e6f94ddce4bea turns the galaxy restriction input into a populated picker. Its server-side data source selects all enabled galaxies and exports type/description values without applying the Galaxy model's existing visibility policy. The GET add/edit routes make that data reachable to authenticated non-admin template authors. History searches identify this commit, rather than the earlier controller scaffold or later moves/refactors, as the smallest BIC; direct inspection of 66f278bb2be0e8183d56eede615d7cc370f38303 proves the query and exposure are absent there. Tag membership puts introduction after v2.5.36 and in v2.5.37. The referenced d3adfe1a097dd4b403364e9af34e208660eeec1a attempts an organisation/distribution filter but writes the distribution predicate as a PHP boolean expression, leaving the disclosure open in v2.5.39. Commit 8aa2bb6d1af6e8c57c8d8437cf203acb8bce7a53 directly closes the mechanism by using Galaxy::buildConditions(), and v2.5.40 is the first tag containing that effective repair. Because the BIC commit object explicitly credits Claude Opus as co-author and that same commit first wrote the causally flawed unrestricted query, the BIC-only rule yields AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
